citations.assertion: Compatible testator identification from family/date context; birth surname and parents not stated. The readable continuation of Mary Glasgow’s will names her son John Glasgow to manage her property and gives a remainder to Mary Glasgow, described as the widow of deceased Wilson Glasgow, and her heirs. The will is dated 5 April 1822; the recorded probate is 14 October 1822. Mary’s existing Newberry family and the probate four days after her reported gravestone death make Mary, wife of James (Crosier-512), the compatible maintained account. The named son is compatible with John Glasgow-1146; the widow is compatible with Mary McCracken-3711, widow of Wilson Glasgow-1982. These identifications are family-context inferences, not additional relationship clauses. The opening on manuscript page 489 runs below the framing of the inspected scan; the following page begins mid-clause. This is a partial reading, not a complete transcription or complete heir list. A Robert Glasgow witnesses the will and proves it; that role is not a statement that he is a son, and no exact Robert profile is assigned. The readable text neither supplies Mary’s birth surname nor identifies her parents. It does not name Tennessee Robert Glasgow-2769 as Archibald’s son or exclude an omitted heir. No father confidence, attachment, mother, vital field or duplicate decision changes. Mary (Crosier) Glasgow: Compatible testator identification from family/date context; birth surname and parents not stated Reviewed 2026-10-31; FamilySearch South Carolina Probate Records, Bound Volumes, collection1919417, Newberry Will BookH, images248–249.
